request: a simple interactive ascii color mixing engine
thesis: Colour mixing made tangible in text: every cell is a character whose glyph encodes brightness and whose ink encodes the mixed hue, so you watch colours blend out of nothing but punctuation.
job: open the page and immediately see an ascii field with colour in it
pick or dial in source colours (primaries)
add them to the field by clicking or dragging, in controllable amounts
watch overlapping colours mix into new ones, glyph density following brightness
switch the mixing model (light adds, paint subtracts) and see the same drops mix differently
read the mixed colour of a cell (hex / rgb) by hovering or clicking
undo the mess: clear or reset the field

principles: additive mixing (light): R+G=yellow, R+B=magenta, G+B=cyan, all=white
subtractive mixing (pigment): C+M=blue, M+Y=red, C+Y=green, all=dark
mix in linear light, display in sRGB, or midtones turn muddy
mixing is a weighted average of components by amount
steps: store each cell as a vector of amounts, not a finished colour
convert vector to rgb at draw time
derive luminance from the mixed rgb for the glyph
tricks: amounts that accumulate and saturate give satisfying build-up
decay or diffusion makes colours bleed into neighbours
tests: cyan + magenta + yellow paint gives near black
equal R,G,B gives grey, not tinted

principles: glyph density is a brightness ramp
monospace cells have roughly 1:2 aspect so grid cells are tall
colour carries hue, glyph carries value
steps: pick a ramp dark to light
colour the character with the mixed rgb
tricks: render rows as spans or one pre with per-cell spans only where colour changes
line-height near 1 and fixed letter-spacing keep the grid square-ish
use a dark background so bright inks glow
tests: empty cell reads as blank, not noise
full-bright cell reads as densest glyph

principles: direct manipulation: drag on the artwork itself
steps: pointer move while down paints along the stroke
controls change what the next stroke does
tricks: pointer events with capture cover mouse and touch
interpolate between pointer samples so fast drags leave no gaps
tests: a drag changes a line of cells

expectations: it responds to the mouse at once
mixing looks plausible to anyone who has mixed paint

kinds.name: paint-on-grid mixer
kinds.what: choose a primary, drag to drop it into cells, overlaps mix; light/paint toggle

kinds.name: three-slider mixer
kinds.what: R, G, B sliders flood the whole grid with the mix

kinds.name: diffusing inks
kinds.what: drops spread and blend into neighbours over time

descriptions: light primaries red, green, blue; paint primaries cyan, magenta, yellow
swatches show the colour as a glyph too
behaviors: adding more of a colour raises its amount in the cell

descriptions: grid about 56 x 24 on desktop, fewer columns on phones
controls beside or below the grid
behaviors: grid cols shrink to fit the viewport width

anti_keywords.not: a full paint program: layers, undo history, save and load, export
blend-mode menus and colour pickers with HSL dials
anti_keywords.instead: three primaries and a model toggle
accumulate amounts per channel and clamp
every control changes state that the grid shows

checks: dropping red then green on one cell in light mode gives a yellow cell
cyan+magenta+yellow in paint mode gives a dark cell
works at phone width without horizontal scroll
